nodes.label: Hermes SOUL.md target
nodes.rationale: SOUL.md is the live instruction file for Hermes; MEMORY.md is not.

nodes.label: Caveman personification problem
nodes.rationale: Naming a stereotyped character pulls the model into that stereotype manifold, which degrades reasoning, costs persona tokens, and is unusable in production.

nodes.label: Prose tokens outside code blocks
nodes.rationale: Counting code tokens would penalise an agent for correctly producing the requested artifact, and the compression that drives cost and latency is the prose around code.

nodes.label: Additive-compatible scope clause
nodes.rationale: Declaring 'communication style only' lets the file append to existing personas and session contracts without overriding task or safety instructions.

nodes.label: Bias toward measurable success criteria
nodes.rationale: 'Be concise' has no self-check; 'max 16 words per sentence' does, which is why hard caps beat soft phrasing.

nodes.label: Output-side compression thesis
nodes.rationale: Input tokens got cheap via prompt caching while output stays billed at full rate and drives latency and reader attention, so compression effort belongs on the output side.

nodes.label: Input/output cost asymmetry under caching
nodes.rationale: Cached input costs ~10% of uncached, so a 9KB prompt pays for itself within about three turns.

nodes.label: Describe the discipline, not a character
nodes.norm_label: describe the discipline, not a character
nodes.rationale: Persona conditioning drags competence and trust; specifying a senior-engineer register keeps the density without the character.

nodes.label: Introspection instructions ineffective
nodes.rationale: Self-reflection prompts produced introspection theatre without measurable compression.

nodes.label: Net-negative workloads
nodes.rationale: Terse replies and per-request billing mean the fixed input overhead exceeds the output saved, so prompt-only install or off is correct.

nodes.label: Output-style instruction only
nodes.rationale: It compresses prose output only; input, context, files and thinking tokens are untouched, so reductions cannot be read as bill savings.

nodes.label: No telemetry, local writes only
nodes.rationale: Installer makes no network calls over its own code path except a pinned, SHA-256-verified fallback fetch.

nodes.label: Codex chain-of-thought inflation
nodes.rationale: Codex prints reasoning to stdout, so the tokenizer counts it as prose; codex numbers overstate bloat until a stripper exists.

nodes.label: v0.14 partial-coverage caveat
nodes.rationale: Negative per-harness reductions reflect more tldr cells than baseline cells (environment gaps), not a TLDR regression.

nodes.label: Prompt self-bloat dilution
nodes.rationale: v0.11's longer anti-metadata rule regressed the total because marginal rules dilute earlier ones; leaner prompt won.

nodes.label: Char count non-monotonic with compliance
nodes.rationale: Past ~1500 chars extra rules reduce compliance; the smallest variant peaked on composer-2-fast.

nodes.label: Cwd contamination
nodes.rationale: Cursor and gemini embed inspected files into replies, so bench cells need a fresh empty cwd.

nodes.label: Positive directives beat negatives
nodes.rationale: Negatives invite RLHF agents to explain what they are not doing, which adds prose.

nodes.label: Communication-only scope statement
nodes.rationale: Leading with the scope contract pre-empts models reading terseness rules as permission to cut correctness.

nodes.label: Output-only override sub-rule
nodes.rationale: Q13 regex output was being wrapped in fences; an explicit artifact-alone rule fixed it.

nodes.label: Anti-helpfulness rule (v0.9)
nodes.rationale: RLHF rewards 'covering the bases', so unsolicited postscripts had to be forbidden explicitly; this single clause moved cursor compliance 73% to 100%.

nodes.label: Regex-simplicity rule (v0.6)
nodes.rationale: The strict IPv4 regex tokenizes to 58 tokens against a 40-token cap, so agents were producing correct answers that could not fit; simplest-correct unblocked 7/8 agents.

nodes.label: Hermes structural ceiling (87%)
nodes.rationale: Hermes CLI appends a review-diff block and session_id trailer after the LLM finishes, so no prompt-level rule can suppress them.

nodes.label: Anti-metadata rule (v0.10)
nodes.rationale: Forbids session_id/runId/diff-views in output; failed on hermes because the CLI appends them after generation.

nodes.label: Diff-fence rule (v0.13)
nodes.rationale: Agents whose CLI auto-injects diff views were told to fence them so they count as code, not prose.

nodes.label: Brevity constraints improve accuracy
nodes.rationale: Brevity constraints reportedly improved accuracy up to 26pp; verbose output creates more room to err. Not measured on this repo's style-focused bench.

nodes.label: Strict ALL-trials-pass compliance
nodes.rationale: Mean-based compliance would hide variance; production users need reliable compression, not lucky-shot compression.

nodes.label: Structural-vs-prose pivot (v0.3)
nodes.rationale: Structure caps cut markdown but not word count; per-sentence and per-prompt-shape length caps target substance, and both layers are needed (35% alone vs 60%+ together).

nodes.label: Accessibility Affordances (skip link, ARIA roles, focus-visible)
nodes.norm_label: accessibility affordances (skip link, aria roles, focus-visible)

nodes.label: Prompt-length penalty
nodes.rationale: Subtracting for chars above 1500 stops the optimizer from buying score with prompt bloat.

nodes.label: Few-shot examples set the floor
nodes.rationale: Example length anchors output length, so shrinking examples from 70 to 20 words moved real answers proportionally.

nodes.label: Draft-then-halve self-trim rule
nodes.rationale: Approximates an internal revision pass; the model halves before emitting, which tightened borderline cases.

nodes.label: No-augment rule
nodes.rationale: Models add framing prose around bullet lists by training habit; forbidding it removes a recurring bloat pattern.

nodes.label: Gemini lesson (-96% after silence rule)
nodes.rationale: A model that looks uncompressible may only need an explicit rule against the narration its architecture defaults to.

nodes.label: Tool-use silence rule
nodes.rationale: Gemini's agentic exploration is fine; narrating it was the prose cost, so the rule forbids narration rather than tool use.

nodes.label: TLDR.chat.md merged into TLDR.md
nodes.rationale: The two prompts differed only in default cap tightness; a separate file added install friction without behavioural delta.

nodes.label: Prepend-to-user-message injection
nodes.rationale: Only claude exposes --append-system-prompt; prepending gives one uniform injection method across agents, at the documented cost of not matching real memory-file deployment.

nodes.label: Independent cross-family judge
nodes.rationale: A judge from a different model family removes the self-preference bias of same-model judging.

nodes.label: Anti-contrarian pushback rule
nodes.rationale: v0.17.0 pushed back too readily on correct users (cursor agree-rate 0.44); the optimizer learned 'disagree only when clearly warranted' so decisiveness and pushback stop trading off.

nodes.label: TLDR.md at local optimum on metric
nodes.norm_label: tldr.md at local optimum on metric
nodes.rationale: Two independent DSPy runs (n=25 and n=73) found no candidate beating the shipped prompt, so further search was judged metric-bound rather than prompt-bound.

nodes.label: Primacy-placed Override section
nodes.rationale: V1's bluntness directive overrode the override clause; moving Override before Bluntness (lost-in-the-middle) restored 2/2 compliance.

nodes.label: Pre-committed pass criteria
nodes.rationale: Criteria were fixed before the run to prevent post-hoc rationalisation of whichever variant happened to win.

nodes.label: TLDR seed at local optimum
nodes.rationale: 33 candidates across two corpus sizes failed to beat the seed, read as the informative-prose floor rather than prompt ceiling.

nodes.label: Deployment-fidelity optimization loop
nodes.rationale: DSPy's signature template reformats the query in a way memory-file prompts never see, so the loop calls the CLI directly with the candidate as real system prompt.

nodes.label: TLDR.blunt.md retired
nodes.rationale: Blunt rules were merged into the single shipping prompt; reintroducing a parallel blunt file is explicitly disallowed absent product change.
